rationale: The assistant correctly read the hum-then-click pattern from the compressor-side box as pointing to the start relay/overload while explicitly keeping a hard-to-start compressor as the key alternative, matching the hidden truth's genuine uncertainty. It kept all instructions to unplugged checks (socket test, dust clearance), told the customer 'Do not buy a part on the symptom alone', and escalated to an engineer to test relay versus compressor, noting the age/replacement economics. Minor gaps: it never asked whether the compressor was hot to touch or the actual temperatures, and gave no indicative repair cost, which would have helped the homeowner's decision.
